criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: The deck holds the dark staged register and one west key. Slides 9 (person at the fed bunk, contact shadow, gold windrow) and 6 (lit near faces at the rail) are the strongest frames. Four frames miss the 7 descriptor. Slide 8's steer is a smoothed kit model that reads as a toy at full size, the tag is salmon rather than the dusk gold accent, and the rail crosses the body instead of the head coming through it. Slide 7 hangs the page against a flat plum mid-tone wall with no yard or sky. On slide 2 the bunk fills about 15 percent of the frame height under a large dead dark band. Slide 5's cream U slab with a navy inside reads as an abstract sculpture rather than a bunk section. Slide 3 is a flat 2D diagram. Slide 4 puts its labels on dark plates over pens whose cattle are a few pixels tall. The cover is missing the storyboard's blank gold tag and the elevator.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: It reads as one deck. Every rendered frame is the same last-light feedyard, the precast bunk and galvanized rail recur on slides 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9, and the storyboard names MOTIF_EVOLUTION and CAMERA_MOVE, both visible in the contact sheet. Slide 3 is a flat grid map that sits outside the rendered world, and slide 7 lifts to a plum mid-tone that strobes against slides 6 and 8.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral I checked traces to a claim or to compute.py. Slide 2's brackets measure as exactly 2, 1 and 1 sections. On slide 3 Canyon to the ranch centre is 7.0 grid squares, and the ranch square side of about 1.93 miles matches 2,393 acres. The slide 7 quote matches c6 verbatim. Three phrasings are looser than their sources. Slide 1's dek states 'the largest federal award in its history' without the attribution the caption gives it ('The A&M System calls'). Slide 6's headline drops the set ('large feedlots', 1,000+ head capacity) that only the dek carries, on a 30 thousand head margin over Nebraska. 'EACH SQUARE IS ONE MILE' means one square mile. All sources are primary.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened ($9.75M USDA grant, $19.5M total), where (seven miles east of Canyon, beside Nance Ranch) and the scale (135 pens, four planned buildings). The deck never gives a deadline, a meeting or a route for the reader. The close on slide 9 and the caption's last line are rhetorical questions to the Feedlot Research Group with no way to ask them. The AI stake stays abstract: nothing says what AI in a feedlot pen would measure or why a Panhandle reader should care, so the AI half is a topic rather than a story.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover hook 'The pens are counted. The AI isn't.' earns the swipe, slide 2 pays at once, and slide 7 is a declared turn. Two frames could go without loss. Slide 6 (cattle on feed) is context the deck never ties back to the AI question, and slide 8 restates slide 7's absence. The close is the same absence asked a third time rather than a landing.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: The vernacular is regional and specific: feed alley, on feed, Nance Ranch, the Kuhlman brothers, Canyon ranchers, the Panhandle, with no boosterism or doom. It reads machine-made in two places. The 'drawn to illustrate' disclaimer is repeated on 8 of 9 deks. Slide 9's 'The grant is awarded. The AI approaches are a plan.' is clipped to the point of flatness.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The subject (agriculture, cattle) and the Hereford red palette are new. The structure repeats recent decks. The ranch drawn as a square of its own area (slide 3) is no. 45's device from four decks ago ('The squares are equal areas, not the parcel's shape'). A last-light world repeats nos. 46 and 48. A document page frame repeats nos. 47 and 48. The spine is again what a release does NOT name, as in nos. 46, 47 and 48, the shape the topics ledger has asked runs to stop leaning on since no. 11.

one_sentence_fix: Merge slides 7 and 8 into one absence frame, and use the freed slot for c23/c24, the 2019 AgriLife cameras-and-AI work on a different Panhandle research feedlot, captioned as not WT's yard. That shows the reader what 'AI-powered approaches' has concretely meant in a Texas feedyard and gives the closing question a stake and a precedent to hold WT to.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The kit steer is smoothed and toy-like at full size, the tag is salmon rather than dusk gold, the rail crosses the body rather than the head coming through it, and the bunk lip and windrow the storyboard promised are missing from the bottom third.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Move the camera to 1.0 m off and lower so the neck rail crosses in front of the face with the head pushed through it. Crop at the poll and dewlap. Add a hair normal map and a rim light on the poll. Set the tag to #E0956A. Bring the grimed bunk lip and the lit windrow into the lower left.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The page hangs against a flat plum mid-tone wall with no sky, no yard and no throat under it. It is the deck's one grey-middle frame and fails the stage test.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Pull the camera back to show the dark bunk throat and concrete back wall under the page, and replace the backdrop with the deck's near black lastLight sky and its ember seam, so the page is the only lit plane.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The four-section bunk fills about 15 percent of the frame height inside a large empty dark band, so the subject does not own the frame.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Drop the eye to 0.6 m and narrow the long lens so the sections span the full width and fill a third of the frame height. Raise the bunk to sit directly under the dek, with the brackets just below it.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The cream U slab with a navy interior reads as an abstract sculpture, not a precast feed bunk section on dunnage.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Turn the section so its J profile and the throat interior take the key, with grime on the lip and a lit bounce in the throat instead of flat navy. Make the dunnage blocks visible pine with contact marks.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The labels sit on dark plates, and the cattle and near triplet are too small at 30 m to read as pens.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Lower the camera to about 15 m over the near triplet so its cattle and bunk read, and set the two labels light on the dark field without plates.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The far 17 steers dissolve into the dark, so the 5-of-22 isotype the dek promises can't be counted at feed size.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Add a low rim light from the seam along the far line so all 22 heads stay separable as dark forms, and make the Texas pen divider a lit pipe.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The cover is missing the storyboard's blank gold tag and the elevator on the seam, and the nearest steer's face is turned into the rail, so the hook's AI half has no image.
artwork_weakest_frames.change: Turn the nearest steer's white face toward the camera with the dusk gold blank tag in its near ear, and place the elevator silhouette on the horizon seam.
